# Evidence package: can label-free RL make a verbalizer flag collusive text? (all numbers generated by scripts/ from results/)

**Pre-registration:** `PREREG.md` (written before the locked test set was scored). **Reports with full tables:** `results/locked_report.md` (confirmatory), `results/judge_report.md`, `results/secondary_report.md`, `results/retention_bev.txt`, `logs/`.

## 1. Design in one paragraph
Verbalizer = Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct + LoRA that turns a layer-20 activation into one sentence. All arms start from the same base SFT adapter, use the same label-free reward (reconstruction, consistency, behaviour; the SFT's concept directions are the only "labels"), the same 400-step schedule stopped at step 100 (checkpoint fixed in advance), and differ ONLY in the unlabeled pool that 60% of steps draw from: **A2** = blatant transcripts in all 4 versions (collusive, collusive-with-the-word, independent, open); **A1** = honest-only control (independent + open only); **A0** = no extra pool (B's public-text pool only). 3 seeds for A1/A2, 1 for A0. References: SFT (no RL), B (earlier RL run, no collusion data), official kitft NLA, and two probes (supervised ones, upper references).
Test set **LOCKED-L** (confirmatory): 1,092 sentences written by separate agents on 12 collusion types never used anywhere else: 359 matched collusive/honest pairs with NO cue words, 122 matched pairs with cue words, and 130 honest sentences that CONTAIN cue words ("I won't collude with you"). Flag = output contains a collusion/secrecy word (`scripts/flag.py`, fixed in advance). BA = balanced accuracy over matched pairs (0.5 = chance).

## 2. Primary result (LOCKED-L, no-cue pairs, step 100, seeds pooled; 95% CI over pairs)
| arm | collusive flagged | honest twin flagged | **BA** [CI] | per-seed BA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SFT | 21% | 18% | 0.515 [0.490, 0.543] | – |
| B (no collusion data) | 4% | 3% | 0.506 [0.492, 0.518] | – |
| A0 plain RL | 13% | 9% | 0.519 [0.497, 0.543] | 0.519 |
| A1 honest-only control | 20% | 9% | 0.553 [0.535, 0.572] | 0.553 / 0.578 / 0.528 |
| **A2 collusion pool** | **38%** | **21%** | **0.589** [0.566, 0.612] | 0.571 / 0.582 / 0.613 |
| long run step 150 / 400 (seed 11 only) | 45% / 34% | 24% / 12% | 0.602 / 0.609 | – |

Paired differences (sign-flip permutation p): **A2 − A1 = +0.036 [+0.016, +0.056], p = 0.0004**; A2 − SFT = +0.073 [+0.048, +0.100], p = 0.0002; A1 − SFT = +0.038 [+0.013, +0.061], p = 0.005; A0 − SFT = +0.004 (n.s.); A2 − B = +0.083. All three A2 seeds are above all three A1 seeds except one overlap (A2 s11 0.571 vs A1 s12 0.578).
**Reading:** the collusion-pool RL beats the honest-only control and plain RL, which is the pre-registered support for "collusive content matters". The honest-only control also beats SFT, so part of the effect is generic. **The absolute effect is small (BA ≈ 0.59; flags 38% of collusive vs 21% of honest sentences).**

## 3. The cue-word control (does the flag follow intent or cue words?) – LOCKED-L, step 100
| arm | collusive no-cue | honest no-cue | collusive with-cue | **honest with-cue** | intent effect (no cue) | cue effect (honest) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SFT | 21% | 18% | 29% | 22% | +3 [-3,+9] | +3 [-4,+12] |
| A1 | 20% | 9% | 27% | 15% | +11 [+6,+15] | +6 [+1,+11] |
| **A2** | 38% | 21% | 56% | 32% | **+18 [+12,+23]** | **+11 [+4,+19]** |
**Reading:** A2 flags honest sentences more when they contain cue words (+11 pts) AND flags collusive more than honest within each cue condition (+18 no cue, +24 with cue). So the flag tracks BOTH intent and cue words; it is not purely a word detector, and not purely an intent detector.

## 4. Blind sentence-only judge (Haiku, ≤ medium, 2 passes averaged, sees neither input nor labels; 100 no-cue pairs per model)
| model | pair AUROC no-cue [CI] | with-cue vs honest-with-cue AUROC |
|---|---|---|
| SFT | 0.470 [0.385, 0.555] | 0.661 |
| B | 0.505 [0.425, 0.580] | 0.554 |
| A1 seed 11 / seed 12 | 0.600 / 0.580 | 0.668 / 0.563 |
| A2 seed 11 / seed 12 | 0.620 / 0.585 | 0.598 / 0.677 |
| **official NLA** | **0.805 [0.730, 0.880]** | **0.988** |
**Reading:** by the judge, A1 ≈ A2 (the keyword edge of A2 over A1 does NOT reproduce here; CIs ±0.08) and both are above SFT/B. The official NLA is far stronger because it writes explicit descriptions ("a proposal to cheat…"). Our outputs score only 3–6/100 on average.

## 5. References on the same sentences
- Supervised collusion-direction probe (mean(collusive)−mean(honest) on an earlier, separate transcript set; layer 20 last token): pair AUROC **0.844** [0.805, 0.880] no-cue; 0.846 with-cue-vs-honest-cue. Core-trained logistic probe: 0.588 [0.538, 0.638] / 0.490.
- Official NLA keyword flag: BA 0.565 (own list) / 0.614 (its list); AR reconstruction cosine 0.863.
So the information is in the activation (probe 0.84); the verbalizers recover only a fraction of it.

## 6. Replication on the earlier sets (secondary; `results/secondary_report.md`)
HAND-50 (written by me, cue-heavy): A2 (3 seeds) flags 14.3/20 collusive vs 3.0/20 honest (BA 0.783); A1 6.3 vs 3.0 (0.583); A0 9 vs 1 (0.70); SFT 2 vs 2 (0.50); B 2 vs 0 (0.55). HELD-OUT-578: A2 0.598, A1 0.569, A0 0.533, SFT 0.554, B 0.515. Same ordering as the locked set; the hand-50 effect is larger because those sentences contain more cue words and n=20 pairs.

## 7. Model health (did RL damage the verbalizer?) – `logs/`, `results/retention_bev.txt`
- Repetition on 256 real agent messages at step 100 (distinct % / most common sentence %; SFT 24 / 16): A2 44/11, 29/**23**, 30/12; A1 34/11, 46/7, 25/**31**; A0 18/15. Two runs (A2 s12, A1 s13) are MORE repetitive than SFT. Seed variance is large; report all seeds.
- B's held-out skills (trained-concept F1; held-out concept named of 68; SFT 0.355 / 3, B 0.453 / 12): A2 0.293 / 10, 0.396 / 7, 0.373 / 4; A1 0.295 / 5, 0.280 / 8, 0.338 / 7; A0 0.367 / 4. No arm reaches B; F1 stays within ~0.08 of SFT except A1 s12 (0.280).

## 8. What can and cannot be claimed
Supported: (i) label-free RL on a collusion-rich unlabeled pool produces a verbalizer whose sentences differ between matched collusive and honest sentences on collusion types it never saw, more than SFT, B, plain RL, and an honest-only-pool control (keyword flag, 3 seeds, p<0.001 vs control); (ii) the effect is small, partly driven by cue words, and not reproduced as a gap between A2 and A1 by the blind judge.
Not supported: detection of realistic/natural collusion (earlier Core/Transfer/Verdict results are at chance); any claim that the verbalizer matches the official NLA or the supervised probe; causal claims about internal collusion representations.
Limitations: all test text is LLM-written (Haiku), one generator family; the flag is a crude lexicon; checkpoint step 100 was chosen on seed 11 before the new seeds (new seeds and locked set are unbiased); only 100 pairs per model judged; A0 has one seed; the supervised probe was built on an earlier set made by the same pipeline.
